contexts.text: The Angels with the man then begin to labour. AC 270.

By work is signified that they could not, except with labour and difficulty, perceive what was true... It is the work and labour of our hands when men must inquire what is true, and do what is good, from self or proprium.
All the labour, etc. () = the Knowledges of faith.
Some thirty = ... that he has laboured but little.
They laboured to find the door () = that they could not see any truth which led to good.
The reason to serve = study, is that the labour which is of the external man is study in the internal. Hence study is called the labour of the mind.
To serve = labour and study; which, when predicated of the Lord, = Own power. AC 3977.
God hath made me forget all my labour () = removal after temptations... Labour = combats, thus temptations.
The land of Egypt laboured... ()... = desolation.
Then the spiritual life labours.
That he labours with every work. Signified.
The Spirits... labour in every way to withdraw them from truth and good.
To labour to drink () = not to want to be instructed...
Work = the labours and studies which have as an end the things of the world.
Labour in temptations. Signified. For in these they who are being tempted have labour against falsities and evils; and the Angels also have labour with them in order that they may be kept in faith...

Six days thou shalt labour, and do all thy work () = the combat which precedes and prepares for this conjunction... To labour and do all one's work = to perform those things which are necessaries of life; here, of the spiritual life...
The Lord has labour with man before he is regenerated. Signified.
Then the Lord has labour; for he fights for man against the Hells...
Under Calf, see this reference.
To labour = to serve.
But when a man is in internal things, then, because he is in Heaven with the Lord, labour and combat cease... This is signified by the seventh day.

Because by the six days of labour... is signified every state of combat; for labour, in the spiritual sense, is not labour such as there is in the world, but such as there is with those who are in the Church, before they enter into the Church, and become the Church; which labour is combat against evil and the falsities of evil. The Lord had the like labour... when He was in the world...
The poor who are content with their lot... love labour more than idleness.
Thy labour, and endurance () = their study and patience.
For My name's sake hast laboured... () = the study and work of procuring for themselves... the things which are of religion and its doctrine.
(In that cavern) all labour; and, as they labour, food is given them from Heaven.
That they may rest from their labours () = ... that those who afflict their soul, and crucify their flesh in the world, for the sake of the Lord and eternal life, will have peace in the Lord.
Such affliction is meant by labour in the following passages. Illustrated.
By the labour which shall be no more () are signified temptations.
They are thrust into an infernal prison, where they are kept labouring for a garment and for food, and after that for some coins...

Six days shalt thou labour... in the natural sense, means that six days are for man and his labours... When the Lord came into the world... the seventh day was made a day of instruction in Divine things, and thus also a day of rest from labours...

By the six days of labour, in the spiritual sense, is signified combat against the flesh and its concupiscences; and at the same time against the evils and falsities which are with one's self from Hell... That so long as this combat lasts, the man has spiritual labour... References.
That the Lord's combats were labours, and are called labours. Illustrated.
In that cave... they are driven to labour for food.
They regard those who... are laborious... as nothing.
In the Hells all are driven to works, and they who do not work receive no food, garments, or bed; thus are they driven to labours.

I know thy works, and thy labour, and thine endurance = all things which they will, think, and do; thus all things of love and faith in the spiritual and in the natural man... Labour = the things which are of thought and faith.
(Thus) by works, in the spiritual sense, is meant all that which man wills and loves; and by labour, all that which man thinks or believes...
The reason why by labour, in the spiritual sense, are meant all things which man thinks, is that to labour spiritually is to think.

For My name's sake hast laboured = the acknowledgement of the Lord and of the Knowledges of truth which regard Him... To labour = to apply the mind and study, that these things may be known and acknowledged; for this signifies to labour, when it is said of those who study the Knowledges of truth and good.
By the labour of his hands which he should eat () is signified study of life according to these things.
The labour of justice () = good conjoined with truth, in which there is peace; for labour, in the Word, is said of truth...
The Church is called labouring () from the study to do what is good.
His combats with the Hells, and their subjugation, is signified by the labour of His soul ().
When the equilibrium is perishing, the Heavens... begin to labour...
By silver is here signified truth from proprium, or Own intelligence; in like manner by labour ().
By labour () is signified the Lord's combat against the Hells, and the subjugation of them, in order that a new Church might be established. AE 695:17.
That they may rest from their labours = that they no longer have any combat against evils and falsities, or infestation by them.
The reason why by labours are meant temptations, is that temptations are labours of the soul, or spiritual labours. Illustrated.
